Trying to drive down your cholesterol by changing your diet can be frustrating. You swap out regular bacon for turkey bacon, eat more oatmeal, and at the end of the day it might not even make a dent in your LDL levels. And yet, dietary interventions seem to work wonders for some people. While it’s tempting to chalk up stubborn cholesterol numbers to genetics, a new study published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology is complicating the picture.   Powered By 10 ShareNextStay“We have people who come into the clinic and say, ‘I changed my diet, and it made no difference in my cholesterol,’” study author Shoa Clarke of Stanford University said in a statement. “Or they say, ‘I changed my diet, and it had a huge effect on my cholesterol.’” Read more: “Iron Is the New Cholesterol”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
